title: Burnley relegated from Premier League: What went wrong, and what now for Scott Parker?
content:
Burnley have been relegated from the Premier League following their 1-0 defeat to Manchester City on Wednesday.

The result means that Burnley, on 20 points with four rounds of matches remaining, cannot reach 17th-place West Ham United’s tally of 33 points.

Burnley’s relegation comes two days after that of Wolverhampton Wanderers, who have been bottom of the table since August and whose demotion was confirmed after West Ham’s goalless draw at Crystal Palace on Monday.

It means Burnley have now been relegated in each of their three most recent campaigns in England’s top flight, having also been relegated in 2021-22 and 2023-24, before earning automatic promotion from the second tier the following season.

Head coach Scott Parker was appointed in the summer of 2024 after Vincent Kompany’s move to Bayern Munich, and led the club to a second-place Championship finish with 100 points and just 16 goals conceded in 46 league games.

However, Burnley have been unable to replicate their defensive solidity in the Premier League; Parker’s side have conceded a league-high 68 goals.

Burnley won three of their opening nine Premier League matches, with home victories over Sunderland and Leeds United followed by an away win at Wolves. However, a 3-2 win at Crystal Palace in February has been their only top-flight victory since October, seeing them cut adrift alongside Wolves.

Parker, 45, has won promotion to the Premier League with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, but has been unable to replicate that success in English football’s top division. He has overseen relegations at Fulham and Burnley in those first seasons back, while Bournemouth parted company with him after a 9-0 defeat at Liverpool, the fourth matchday of the 2022-23 season.

Burnley still have four league games remaining, with visits to Leeds United (May 1) and Arsenal (May 17) either side of a home game against Aston Villa (May 10), before they host Wolves on the final day of the season, on May 24.

Analysis by Andy Jones

For many Burnley fans, the writing has been on the wall long before Wednesday’s defeat.

After top-flight failure under Kompany two years ago, Burnley returned to the Premier League under Parker with the aim of doing things differently.

Their recruitment, which had been centred around young players in 2023, this time included experienced players and those who had been on loan during the previous campaign. The style was also different with Parker, who oversaw a record-breaking defence in the Championship and a pragmatism not seen under his predecessor, whose sides produced free-flowing football.

While there were early signs that they were much more prepared to fight for survival, one win in their last 25 Premier League games tells its own story. They have lacked creativity and firepower in attack, the sturdy defence of last season has been non-existent, and in a number of matches they have looked devoid of belief from the start.

Not all fans were convinced by Parker when he guided them to promotion last season, but the frustration with him and the club’s owners ALK Capital, led by Alan Pace, has increased as the season has gone on. Despite that, the head coach has remained in his position.

They have become the Premier League’s latest yo-yo club, and the challenge is to earn promotion again in what looks set to be a very competitive Championship next season.

Decisions need to be made on whether they try and keep as much of the squad together as possible following multiple summers of upheaval, and ultimately whether they continue with Parker who has shown he excels at getting teams into the Premier League, but keeping them up is a different story.
